video_credit_ledger.scope: Legacy Film Room credits owned by teams.id. It is neither per-user nor club_program-scoped and has no product discriminator.
video_credit_ledger.balance: Derived on every read as SUM(delta) filtered only by team_id; there is no separate balance service or cached balance.

movements.debit: POST /admin/video/matches/<id>/process inserts -1 for legacy team matches, atomically with job creation and queued status.
movements.grant: Admin endpoint accepts any non-zero signed delta and any declared reason.
movements.refund: Admin endpoint inserts +1 once per video_match_id/reason=refund, but does not verify that a debit exists.
movements.purchase: Unimplemented: purchase is an allowed reason and stripe_session_id is unique, but no origin/main code writes either.

video_credit_ledger.admin_only: All balance, grant, refund, and processing routes use require_api_key. Club managers can request processing, but club_program matches explicitly bypass the ledger and debit.
dead_or_incomplete: No customer checkout or Stripe webhook grants video credits.
The concierge grant comment still says Stripe purchases arrive in a future phase.
Locking the match row does not serialize two concurrent debits against the same team balance.
video_credit_ledger.generalisation_assessment: Generalising this table in place would require nullable/polymorphic ownership, product filters on every existing balance query, and backfilling legacy team rows. That is larger and riskier than isolating user-owned GOL credits.

reuse_from_s3: BillingCustomer and ensure_customer can be reused unchanged for one customer per user.
Stripe signature verification, StripeWebhookEvent event-id claiming, terminal duplicate handling, failed-event persistence, retry locking, and transaction commit/rollback can be reused unchanged.
BillingCheckoutSession's user scope, client_key idempotency, Stripe session id, URL, expiry, and open/complete/expired lifecycle are reusable.
The BILLING_ENABLED dark gate is reusable: disabled can preserve unlimited beta access; enabled activates allowance and credits.
The billing route, authentication, rate limit, Stripe price lookup, portal route, and admin-summary endpoint can remain.
Subscription watermarking and upsert logic remain useful only for existing or future recurring Scout Pro products; payment purchases do not need subscription watermarks.
Existing subscription MRR/status fields in admin_summary can remain, while webhook-health and open-checkout counts already cover both modes.
must_change: Add server-defined GOL packs to PRODUCT_CATALOG with purchase_mode=payment and an authoritative integer credit quantity. Do not accept credit quantity or price from client metadata.
Make /billing/config describe payment packs without synthesising month/year intervals; expose mode, pack/price code, displayed amount, and granted credits.

Branch create_checkout by catalog mode. Payment mode must skip active_subscription/already_subscribed checks, use mode=payment, omit subscription_data, and attach kind=credit_topup, product_code=gol, pack_id, and user_id metadata to both Session and PaymentIntent.
Do not run subscription duplicate-cancellation logic for payment sessions. Two genuinely completed top-ups are both purchases and must both grant credits.

On paid checkout.session.completed, resolve the persisted checkout/user, lock the user row, mark the checkout complete, and insert the grant in the same webhook transaction. A unique nullable stripe_session_id on the GOL ledger provides a second idempotency boundary behind StripeWebhookEvent.
Either restrict Checkout to immediate-payment methods or also handle checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded; an unpaid completed event must not grant credits.

Persist stripe_payment_intent_id and amount_paid_cents on grants so charge.refunded can find the purchase and compute cumulative proportional reversals. Out-of-order refunds should fail retryably rather than be silently discarded.
Extend admin_summary additively with GOL gross purchases, refunded amount, credits granted/spent/outstanding, and negative-balance count.
Extend /billing/me or /auth/me with free_questions_remaining and credit_balance; the existing panel does not fetch /billing/me.

Replace require_scout_entitlement("gol_chat") on /gol/chat with the allowance/credit reservation. Otherwise free users cannot consume their three questions. Remove that gate from export-pdf unless exporting an already-created conversation is also meant to cost credit.

Detach gol_chat from subscription/grandfather entitlement semantics, or explicitly migrate any real legacy Scout Pro subscribers to credits. Omitting subscription price envs prevents new checkout offers but does not stop existing subscription rows from granting GOL today.
Require a stable client_msg_id per submitted question. session_id is conversation-wide and cannot prevent double-debit on a retried turn.
Teach useGolChat/APIService about HTTP 402 credits_exhausted and about a usage SSE event so balances update immediately after a successful reservation or refund.
Refactor GolService error handling or inspect its emitted error event: GolService currently catches provider failures and yields error, so the route's exception handler alone cannot trigger a refund.
gol_question_boundary: One POST /api/gol/chat is one billable question. message is the new user turn; history only replays up to 20 earlier messages. Every follow-up sends another POST and therefore consumes another allowance unit or credit. A single question can cause up to six LLM completion calls through tool recursion at depths 0 through 5.

Lock UserAccount, idempotency-check client_msg_id, then commit either a free-bucket debit or prepaid debit before the first LLM call.

out_of_credits_shape.reason: It must be returned before SSE headers are committed; an error emitted inside generate() is necessarily an HTTP 200 stream.

what_nbhd_decided: CreditLedger is append-only and tenant-owned, with kinds grant, debit, reversal, and adjustment.
Amounts are signed Decimal USD; Tenant.purchased_credit is a denormalised hot-read balance, while the ledger is the audit trail.
Packs are server-defined CREDIT_PACKS. Clients select only pack_id; checkout and webhook both re-derive price and granted credit.
Checkout uses mode=payment and metadata kind=credit_topup, pack_id, tenant_id, user_id on both Session and PaymentIntent.
checkout.session.completed and checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded route payment credit top-ups separately from subscriptions.
charge.refunded matches the grant by PaymentIntent and computes an incremental reversal from Stripe's cumulative amount_refunded.
Grant/reversal idempotency uses stripe_event_id partial unique constraints; the grant also records session id, PaymentIntent, pack id, and amount paid.
Per-turn idempotency vocabulary is client_msg_id, unique within the tenant.
The exhaustion error vocabulary is budget_exhausted. There is no per-question free-allowance pattern: nbhd uses a monthly included dollar budget plus persistent purchased credit.
nbhd clamps refunds at zero and absorbs already-spent value. That policy should not be copied accidentally because its ledger sum can diverge from the clamped hot balance.

mirror_where_sensible.table_vocabulary: kind=grant|debit|reversal|adjustment, stripe_event_id, stripe_session_id, stripe_payment_intent_id, pack_id, amount_paid_cents
mirror_where_sensible.error_code: Use credits_exhausted for loanarmy's question-credit model; nbhd's budget_exhausted describes a materially different monthly-dollar budget.

recommendation.ledger_detail: Create an append-only user-scoped gol_credit_ledger rather than altering VideoCreditLedger. Use signed integer delta, bucket=free_allowance|prepaid, kind=grant|debit|reversal|adjustment, unique idempotency_key, nullable unique stripe_session_id, PaymentIntent, pack, amount-paid, and timestamps. Prepaid balance is SUM(delta) in the prepaid bucket.
recommendation.free_allowance: lifetime — model the policy as an implicit opening balance of 3 and append free_allowance debits/refunds keyed by client_msg_id; remaining=max(0, 3 + SUM(free bucket delta)). This is retry-safe, auditable, requires no reset job, and avoids timezone ambiguity.
recommendation.checkout: Expose a server-defined $20 GOL starter pack plus owner-approved top-up packs, all using Checkout mode=payment. The number of questions granted per pack remains a business input and must be configured server-side.
recommendation.refunds: Record cumulative proportional reversals against the original PaymentIntent. Allow prepaid balance to become negative when refunded credits were already spent, block further paid questions, and make later top-ups clear the deficit first. This preserves ledger truth and prevents refund-after-use abuse.
recommendation.failure_policy: Reserve before the LLM call. Append an idempotent compensating adjustment if the server/provider ends without a done event; do not refund client cancellation/disconnect. Admin and BILLING_ENABLED=false calls bypass both free usage and prepaid debit.

risks: Retried or concurrently duplicated streams double-debit without a client_msg_id unique boundary; session_id cannot serve because it spans the conversation.
A debit commits before the generator starts. Provider/tool failures must create an idempotent compensating entry, while client aborts must not become a free-use exploit.
GolService swallows exceptions into SSE error events, so refund logic must observe terminal events rather than rely only on raised exceptions.

Current signed admin role bypass and billing-disabled beta behavior must be checked before allowance consumption. Grandfathered users and any existing Scout Pro subscribers need an explicit migration policy.
If the owner later changes to a daily allowance, use a canonical naive-UTC date consistently; server-local dates would reset differently across deployments. Lifetime allowance avoids this issue.
Refunds after spend require an explicit negative-balance versus platform-loss policy. Clamping without a separate liability field destroys SUM-ledger balance truth.
One question credit can fund up to six LLM calls. Pack economics must use worst-case tool recursion or cap/model the rounds; charging per internal call would violate the promised per-question unit.
HTTP 402 must occur before streaming begins. Once SSE starts, only an event:error inside an HTTP 200 response is possible.
Delayed payment methods require async_payment_succeeded support; otherwise paid customers may never receive credit.
Partial refunds require cumulative-to-incremental conversion and deterministic integer-credit rounding.
SQLite ignores real SELECT FOR UPDATE behaviour. Existing SQLite tests can verify shapes and uniqueness but cannot prove concurrent allowance/debit safety; add a PostgreSQL concurrency test.
The existing VideoCreditLedger has a same-team race because it locks VideoMatch, not Team. Reusing that pattern for GOL would permit overspending.
